To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ultrasound measured renal length and low dose CT measured renal volume were repeatable; (2) there was a strong correlation between ultrasound measured renal length, low dose CT measured volume and single kidney glomerul filtration rate; and (3), low dose CT measured volumes were more strongly correlated to single kidney glomerur filtration rate than ultrasound measured length.

(1) low dose CT volume is a better surrogate marker for single kidney glomular filtration rate than length; (2) ultrasound measurements of length, area and thickness are a better predictor of low dose CT volume and glomerular filtration than length on its own; (3) ultrasound length and low dose CT volume are both repeatable.
